Consigned to His Excellency, the High and Noble, Strict, and greatly esteemed Lord Jacob Mossel, Governor General, and the Noble and esteemed Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies.

No. 1. Original letter to the well-mentioned His High Excellency by the Resident here under today's date directed.

From Palembang, the 28th of February, 1751.

No. 2. Copy letter, from and to as above, dated the 20th of September in the year 1780.

No. 3. Two copies of resolutions dated the 16th of January and the 17th of February, passed here in council, and also given orders to the steersman Abraham Meershoek dated the 16th and 19th of January, filed under letters A and B.

No. 4. [blank]

No. 5. Copy letter from the steersman Meershoek, several times, dated the 22nd of January of the past year, directed to the chief here, resolved, together with a report by the commissioners concerning the aforementioned.

No. 6. From Palembang, the 28th of February, 1751. Incidents concerning Raja Allam handed over to the chief aforementioned, dated the 28th of January and the 2nd of February of this year.

No. 7. The double requisition of necessities for the year 1752/1753, annexed with catalogues of the needed medicines.

No. 8. Two pieces of petitions, at the request to be discharged from the service of the Company and to be placed in citizen freedom by His High Excellency, the High Indian government.

No. 9. Original report by the chief surgeon of this Company concerning the condition of the Company's slaves at Palembang, the 28th of February, 1751, handed over to the chief here.

High and Noble, Strict, greatly esteemed, Earnest, valiant, wise, prudent, and most generous Lord and Lords.

We found ourselves upon the return of the King's envoy, the Temenggong Surah Mengala, newly gladdened with Your High Excellency's greatly esteemed letter dated the 14th of September of the year in question, by which we were at the same time most graciously informed of the death of the High and Noble, well-born Lord Gustaf Willem Baron van Imhoff, and that in his place, to the high and important and eminent dignity of Governor General of these Indian territories, was elected His High Excellency, greatly esteemed, at the head of this aforementioned. With this glorious and much-desired succession, we felicitate His High Excellency, greatly esteemed, by these means from the depths of our souls. May Jehovah's fiery providence deign to bless the dear person of the well-mentioned His High Excellency, greatly esteemed, with a span of years with perfect health and a fortunate reign, mildly for the welfare of this Dutch company and all its servants. Furthermore, upon the aforementioned greatly esteemed letter, we have learned with bitter heartfelt sorrow the displeasure of Your High Excellency, greatly esteemed, with respect to the first undersigned, caused by the continuous fabricated complaints of this king, concerning whom the first undersigned, during his presence here, on the contrary has shown all possible

In the month of December, Raja Alang, or so-called King of Siantang, who in the past year had been driven from his unlawful possession by the King of Johor and has since been occupied with murder and piracy around Borneo, Billiton, and hereabouts, came to settle on the island of Banca with 22 vessels and approximately 300 persons strong. From Palembang, the 28th of February, 1751. Of the inhabitants of which, who consist in great part of Siantangers, he immediately knew how to draw a good many to his side, and thus his following grew so much that the same soon found himself very strong there, and consequently too powerful to be driven from there by force by the Palembanger, whose bloody and lascivious nature had been sufficiently known to him from early times.
